notes.1a: ,(b) The majority of candidates determined the volume and the mass of the sand.
notes.1c: Most candidates correctly calculated the density of sand. The most common error was to write an incorrect equation for calculating density.
notes.1d: Most candidates were awarded full credit. Weaker answers gave explanations in terms of gold mixing with the sand.
notes.2ai: The majority of candidates determined the correct distance from the graph.
notes.2aii: The majority of candidates gained most of the available credit. A common mistake was failing to convert the time from minutes to seconds, or using an incorrect time from the graph.
notes.2b: The majority of candidates scored full credit.
notes.3a: ,(b) The majority of candidates scored full credit.
notes.3c: Only the strongest candidates gained the majority of the available credit. notes.4a: Most candidates were awarded credit. The most common mistake was to only give a description for part of the day.
notes.4b: The strongest candidates scored full credit. Weaker candidates did not link the ideas of temperature increase, increased molecular motion and more frequent or harder collisions with the wall of the balloon.
notes.5a: This was one of the best-answered questions on the paper, with the majority of candidates gaining full credit.
notes.5b: Candidates found this a challenging question. The majority of candidates only gave one or two benefits of renewable energy sources, and weaker candidates merely listed other examples of renewable energy sources.
notes.6ai: &(ii) Most candidates gained full credit. Weaker candidates did not name the normal line and did not identify the angle of reflection.
notes.6bi: Most candidates were awarded credit. A common error was to use the colour purple instead of indigo.
notes.6bii: The strongest candidates gained most of the available credit on this question. The majority of candidates did not recognise that total internal reflection would take place because the angle of incidence had increased beyond the critical angle for the semi-circular glass block.
notes.7a: Many candidates recognised that hot air rises, but very few linked this to an expansion of the air or a decrease in the density of the air.
notes.7b: The strongest candidates gained most of the available credit for this question. However, very few candidates linked the properties of aluminium foil as a good reflector or the trapped air as an insulator, reducing thermal energy transfer by conduction and convection.
notes.8a: The strongest candidates were able to describe a suitable method for determining the speed of sound in air.
notes.8bi: The majority of candidates identified the amplitude of the wave. The most common error was to state it was equal to BE.
notes.8bii: The majority of candidates identified the wavelength of the wave. The most common errors were to state it was either AC or AF.
notes.8biii: The majority of candidates did not follow the instruction to draw the wave on Fig. 8.1 . Where possible, credit was given for responses drawn in the space below the question. It would be a useful exercise for candidates to practice drawing a wave on top of an existing wave to demonstrate changes in amplitude and frequency.
notes.9a: The majority of candidates identified one or two uses correctly.
notes.9b: The majority of candidates scored partial credit for a description of the damage caused by X-ray machines, but only the stronger candidates linked the damage to the fact that X-rays are ionising radiation, or the idea of excessive exposure. notes.10a: Stronger candidates gained full credit, but weaker candidates did not state that similar poles of magnets would repel.
notes.10b: The majority of candidates scored most of the credit available for this question. Some candidates misread the question and tried to explain that nothing would happen when the switch was open.
notes.10c: There were many examples of carefully drawn field patterns, including the correct direction of the magnetic field.
notes.11ai: Most candidates were awarded the majority of credit for this question. As expected, the most common error was interchanging of the symbols for the ammeter and the voltmeter.
notes.11aii: Most candidates gained full credit for this question. The most common error amongst some candidates was to mis-state the equation for resistance.
notes.11aiii: The stronger candidates recognised that the resistance of the lamp would increase.
notes.11bi: Most candidates gained full or partial credit for this question.
notes.11bii: Many candidates stated facts that were common to both series and parallel combinations of lamps and therefore could not be awarded credit.
notes.12a: Most candidates were awarded the majority of available credit for this question.
notes.12bi: &(ii) Most candidates gained full credit on this question. Some candidates thought that the number of neutrons was 210.
